newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel army chief to South Africa, Thailand. [Corrected 14:08 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Israel army chief to South Africa, Thailand. [Corrected 14:08 gmt]

text.p: Israeli Army Chief of Staff Amnon Shahak has departed (corrects from "departs on Tuesday") for visits to South Africa and Thailand aimed at strengthening military ties with the two states, the army said.
"Chief of Staff Amnon Lipkin Shahak will pay official visits to South Africa and Thailand," an army spokesman said.

"During his trip he will meet the army chiefs of these states and visit army bases. The visit is meant to strengthen relations between the Israeli Defence Forces and the armies of South Africa and Thailand," the spokesman said.
The army said Shahak was first due in South Africa.
Israel has been worried by a South African proposal to sell tank firing systems to Syria, the Jewish state's arch-foe.

Despite Israel's tight relations with South Africa's former white rulers, the Jewish state has maintained close ties with Pretoria since President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) ended decades of apartheid rule in 1993.
Israel had officially opposed apartheid, but facing world criticism over its treatment of Palestinians, the Jewish state shared a sense of isolation with white-ruled South Africa.
The ANC had for decades identified with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO).
A 1993 Israel-PLO peace deal which coincided with the end of white rule in South Africa paved the way for the thaw in ties between the ANC and the Jewish state.
